title: Break a Retain Cycle with weak

docs.title: ARC — Strong Reference Cycles Between Class Instances

hints: Two objects holding strong references to each other are never freed.
Make the child's back-reference to its parent `weak`.
jsBridge: Parent ↔ child strong references leak under ARC, because neither count reaches zero. JS's GC collects cycles, so JS devs never think about this. In Swift, the child's back-reference must be `weak` (or `unowned`).

compass.q: JS mark-and-sweep GC frees cycles. What does ARC gain in exchange for not doing that?
Java's GC also handles cycles. Name one Swift benefit of ARC (deterministic deinit, no pauses) over GC.
`weak var parent` vs `unowned let parent`: which crashes if you're wrong about lifetimes?
How do you find this leak in Xcode (Memory Graph debugger)? What does it look like?
